# Import complete dataset editions into an existing Rails application

This example turns an original received SF88/SF100 dataset into a reviewed, repeatable database import. It includes the migration, application models, field mapping, background job and commissioning command. The importer keeps the application's existing tenant relation, target records, database connection and native dataset source together.

A complete preview shows every incoming and removed key. Committing that selected preview writes all target changes, current key state, original source rows, edition history and the final receipt in one Active Record transaction. A repeated business operation key reopens its original committed result.

## Install the application side

Use Ruby 3.1 or newer, Rails/Active Record 7.1 or newer and the application's existing database. The merchant package already includes the Ruby standard-library reader and source-bound Dataset receiving client. The application adds Active Record and Active Job through its normal Rails bundle.

Copy the example migration into the application's migration directory with an unused timestamp and run the application's usual migration command. The migration creates four import/history tables and one example target table:

| Table | Stored application state |
| --- | --- |
| starforge_dataset_streams | Tenant/name identity, source/key/scope bindings, current revision and latest edition |
| starforge_dataset_editions | Stable operation identity, selected preview and complete committed receipt |
| starforge_dataset_rows | Current exact source key, original target ID, active/removed state and last source values |
| starforge_dataset_entries | Every edition's original JSON row, exact changes, target ID and source position |
| starforge_dataset_catalog_records | Example tenant-scoped business records with an actual unique source key |

~~~sh
dataset_package=/absolute/customer-package
cp "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/create_dataset_import_tables.rb" \
  db/migrate/20261012085000_create_dataset_import_tables.rb
bin/rails db:migrate
install -d -m 0700 tmp/dataset-review
~~~

Choose a new migration timestamp if that path already exists. Keep the delivered package hierarchy intact: the example models load the verified importer through its relative package path.

For a customer's established schema, keep the four history tables and replace the example CatalogRecord with the application's original model. The relation passed to RailsDataset must already enforce the authenticated tenant's record scope. The stream and all four model classes must use the very same Active Record connection pool. Add or retain a real unique index covering the selected key within that scope; for this example it is tenant_key plus external_id.

The model examples make completed editions and source entries immutable through normal Active Record writes. The stream and current-key state advance as later complete editions are committed. Retain all four history tables with the application's regular database backups.

## Receive the original complete dataset

Follow the merchant package's [Dataset receiving guide](../../DATASETS.md) to prepare, review, acquire or attach, receive, and reopen the original dataset. Retain its actual dataset-customer.json SHA-256 with the application import record.

The Rails side opens that completed directory offline. The receiving reader checks every required original file, whole-file byte count and SHA-256, final native status, full page/row range and projected field set before yielding rows. It parses original integer tokens as Ruby Integer and decimal tokens as BigDecimal; the original JSON spelling and row order remain available for each row.

The same completed packet can be reopened by a background job. Each iteration reads a private immutable verified snapshot. Original payment review, native acquisition and recovery belong to the existing merchant Dataset client.

## Map the customer's real fields

Copy mapping.json into the application's configuration and change its field names to the actual received dataset. Remove unused example mappings. Every mapped source field must appear in the received manifest's projected fields.

The included mapping expects these example source names: id, name, amount, quantity, active, observed_on and recorded_at. Their names are application examples; inspect the actual delivery's fields before selecting them:

~~~ruby
delivery = Starforge::DatasetDelivery.open(
  "/absolute/private/received-dataset",
  expected_manifest_sha256: actual_manifest_sha256
)
puts JSON.pretty_generate(delivery.fields)
~~~

The mapping has three decisions:

| Setting | Result |
| --- | --- |
| key_columns | Exact stable business key; one or several mapped target columns |
| columns | Source field and explicit native target type for each managed attribute |
| removal | Retain missing records, or set a separate Boolean archive column inactive |

Supported target types are string/text, integer, decimal, Boolean, date and datetime. A source integer stays exact. A decimal string or native decimal token is accepted only when the target column preserves its value and range. A datetime must carry an explicit UTC or numeric offset and fit the database column's precision. Date strings use YYYY-MM-DD. Boolean fields accept actual true/false values.

A string column accepts a string by default. Set stringify to true only when the application intentionally converts a numeric or Boolean source value to its literal text. Stable keys retain capitalization, whitespace and leading zeroes supplied as strings.

For each mapping, null is assign or preserve; missing is error or preserve. These are independent choices. Key columns always require an actual value. The original SF100 reader supplies the complete projected row shape, and a field left out of the application's mapping remains application-owned. Explicit null assignments must fit the target column's null constraint. Target primary keys, timestamps, lock versions, STI columns and fixed scope attributes cannot be overwritten by source mapping.

The supplied archive policy uses source_active:

~~~json
{
  "strategy": "archive",
  "column": "source_active",
  "active": true,
  "inactive": false
}
~~~

A key absent from a later complete selected dataset becomes removed in the import state and its original target record receives source_active=false. If the key reappears, its record becomes active and the preview reports restored. With {"strategy":"retain"}, removal changes the import history while preserving the target record's attributes.

Removals are calculated from previously managed active keys in this exact stream. The importer requires the original complete selection: a final native snapshot, original merchant contract, operation, resolved endpoint, selected query and tenant scope. Page cursor, page size and dataset snapshot can change as the same selected dataset advances. Changing the merchant contract, dataset endpoint, key definition or selected membership requires an explicit application migration or another authorized stream.

## Create the stable stream and review the complete edition

Run commissioning through the actual Rails application's runner so the original database and model configuration are loaded. Paths below are templates for the customer's retained package, received delivery, configuration and private output directory.

~~~sh
bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" init -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog

bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" preview -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog \
  --delivery /absolute/private/received-dataset \
  --manifest-sha256 ACTUAL_DATASET_CUSTOMER_MANIFEST_SHA256 \
  --mapping /absolute/application/config/dataset-catalog-mapping.json \
  --out /absolute/application/tmp/dataset-review
~~~

The preview command writes the entire JSON and CSV revision into files named by its full preview SHA-256. It also prints counts and the exact output descriptors. Every preview entry includes:

- Original source ordinal, original JSON line and row SHA-256.
- Exact stable key and existing native target ID.
- Inserted, updated, unchanged or removed action.
- Adopted existing record, restored key and changed-source indicators.
- Exact before/after values and the selected target's current version fingerprint.

The complete JSON uses tagged values for precise types. For example, ["integer","9007199254740993"] is an exact integer, ["decimal","12.34000001"] is an exact decimal, ["null"] is explicit null, and ["datetime","2026-10-12T08:00:00.000000000Z"] is a UTC instant. The original unmodified source JSON is retained beside those mapped values.

Review all changes through these files or embed Preview.each_entry in the application's existing review screen. The neutral JSON/CSV surfaces carry the full dataset; the printed summary provides navigation and the selected hash. No preview is committed by creating or exporting it.

## Apply that selected preview

Use a persistent operation key from the application's own import/job record. Preserve that exact key and preview hash when a job retries.

~~~sh
bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" commit -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog \
  --delivery /absolute/private/received-dataset \
  --manifest-sha256 ACTUAL_DATASET_CUSTOMER_MANIFEST_SHA256 \
  --mapping /absolute/application/config/dataset-catalog-mapping.json \
  --operation catalog-edition-2026-10-12 \
  --preview-sha256 ACTUAL_COMPLETE_PREVIEW_SHA256 \
  --out /absolute/application/tmp/dataset-review
~~~

The importer locks the stream, rebuilds the complete current preview and compares it to the selected hash. It then saves the actual application models using their normal validations and callbacks, verifies the stored mapped values and scope, and commits the target updates plus complete edition history together. A changed target, changed stream revision or changed source/mapping produces a fresh-preview requirement before any edition is applied. Database/model validation failures roll back the whole transaction.

If a process exits after the database commit but before exporting its receipt, the same command with the original operation and preview returns that already committed edition and recreates its complete receipt export. Using that operation key for another source, mapping or preview is rejected.

The importer owns its database transaction boundary. Call it outside another open application transaction. Use database-side work or the application's after_commit/outbox arrangement for external effects in model callbacks. Active Record documents [transaction scope and callback behavior](https://api.rubyonrails.org/v7.1.0/classes/ActiveRecord/Transactions/ClassMethods.html) and [row locking with with_lock](https://api.rubyonrails.org/v7.1.0/classes/ActiveRecord/Locking/Pessimistic.html).

## Use the actual application job

The provided ImportDatasetJob consumes an already received complete packet and selected application preview. Resolve tenant identity and paths within the authenticated application, then enqueue the stable values:

~~~ruby
Starforge::DatasetExample::ImportDatasetJob.perform_later(
  stream_id: stream.id,
  tenant_key: current_account.dataset_tenant_key,
  delivery_directory: import_record.received_directory,
  manifest_sha256: import_record.dataset_manifest_sha256,
  mapping_path: Rails.root.join("config", "dataset-catalog-mapping.json").to_s,
  operation_key: import_record.operation_key,
  preview_sha256: import_record.selected_preview_sha256,
  receipt_path: import_record.receipt_path
)
~~~

Require the delivered job from an application initializer, for example require "/absolute/customer-package/examples/rails_dataset/import_dataset_job". To move it into the application's normal autoload paths, move its model classes with it and update the relative require to their actual location. The importer takes those classes explicitly:

~~~ruby
importer = Starforge::RailsDataset.new(
  delivery: delivery,
  scope: current_account.catalog_records,
  stream: stream,
  models: {edition: DatasetEdition, row: DatasetRow, entry: DatasetEntry},
  mapping: mapping
)
preview = importer.preview
begin
  File.open(review_path, "wb") { |io| preview.write_json(io) }
  selected_hash = preview.sha256
ensure
  preview.close
end
# Persist selected_hash with the application review decision, then use it:
receipt = importer.import!(
  operation_key: import_record.operation_key,
  expected_preview_sha256: import_record.selected_preview_sha256
)
~~~

The source key is resolved against the real scoped target relation. An existing matching record can be adopted once; a record already managed by a different stream is rejected. If a tracked target has moved outside the authorized scope, the application must resolve that relationship before applying another edition. All new records inherit the fixed values from the original scope.

## Reopen a committed edition and continue revisions

The status command reads the current stream and complete active/removed key counts:

~~~sh
bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" status -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog
~~~

The receipt command exports every retained entry from an existing operation, including original source JSON and exact before/after values:

~~~sh
bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" receipt -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog \
  --delivery /absolute/private/received-dataset \
  --manifest-sha256 ACTUAL_DATASET_CUSTOMER_MANIFEST_SHA256 \
  --mapping /absolute/application/config/dataset-catalog-mapping.json \
  --operation catalog-edition-2026-10-12 \
  --out /absolute/application/tmp/dataset-review
~~~

Reopen can use a current complete packet belonging to the same bound stream while exporting an earlier operation's saved source rows. The exporter checks every retained row hash, complete entry count and edition digest. All output writes are streamed into a private temporary file; an interrupted export can be repeated, and an existing path is accepted only when its full bytes match.

For the next original dataset edition, retain the same stream and stable key mapping, receive its complete packet, create a new application operation key, preview its entire diff and commit that selected preview. The existing target identities, source history and application records advance together.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Run through the original Rails application's bin/rails runner.
require "optparse"
require_relative "models"

module Starforge
  module DatasetExample
    module Commission
      module_function
      def run(arguments)
        options = {}
        parser = OptionParser.new do |o|
          o.banner = "bin/rails runner /absolute/package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb COMMAND -- [options]"
          o.separator "Commands: init, preview, commit, receipt, status"
          o.on("--tenant KEY", "Authenticated application's tenant key") { |v| options[:tenant] = v }
          o.on("--stream NAME", "Stable dataset stream within that tenant") { |v| options[:stream] = v }
          o.on("--delivery DIRECTORY", "Original complete received dataset") { |v| options[:delivery] = v }
          o.on("--manifest-sha256 SHA", "Selected dataset-customer.json SHA-256") { |v| options[:manifest] = v }
          o.on("--mapping PATH", "Application's explicit JSON field mapping") { |v| options[:mapping] = v }
          o.on("--out DIRECTORY", "Existing private complete-output directory") { |v| options[:out] = v }
          o.on("--operation KEY", "Stable application edition operation key") { |v| options[:operation] = v }
          o.on("--preview-sha256 SHA", "Exact full preview selected for commit") { |v| options[:preview] = v }
          o.on("-h", "--help") { puts o; return 0 }
        end
        command = arguments.shift
        if command.nil? || %w[-h --help].include?(command)
          puts parser
          return 0
        end
        # Rails runner retains all following arguments; accept its optional
        # delimiter without allowing unknown flags to disappear silently.
        arguments.shift if arguments.first == "--"
        parser.parse!(arguments)
        RailsDataset.need(arguments.empty? && %w[init preview commit receipt status].include?(command),
          "DATASET_COMMISSION_COMMAND")
        required = [:tenant, :stream]
        required += [:delivery, :manifest, :mapping] if %w[preview commit receipt].include?(command)
        required += [:out] if %w[preview receipt].include?(command)
        required += [:operation, :preview] if command == "commit"
        required += [:operation] if command == "receipt"
        required.each do |key|
          RailsDataset.need(options[key].is_a?(String) && !options[key].strip.empty?,
            "DATASET_COMMISSION_OPTION", option: key)
        end
        stream_scope = DatasetStream.where(tenant_key: options[:tenant], name: options[:stream])
        if command == "init"
          # The unique tenant/name index resolves concurrent job creation.
          stream = stream_scope.create_or_find_by!({})
          puts RailsDataset.json({"stream_id"=>stream.id.to_s, "tenant"=>stream.tenant_key,
            "name"=>stream.name, "revision"=>stream.revision})
          return 0
        end
        stream = stream_scope.take!
        if command == "status"
          editions = DatasetEdition.where(dataset_stream_id: stream.id)
          puts RailsDataset.json({"stream_id"=>stream.id.to_s, "tenant"=>stream.tenant_key, "name"=>stream.name,
            "revision"=>stream.revision, "latest_edition_id"=>stream.latest_edition_id&.to_s,
            "target_model"=>stream.target_model, "scope_sha256"=>stream.scope_sha256,
            "key_mapping_sha256"=>stream.key_mapping_sha256, "membership_sha256"=>stream.membership_sha256,
            "editions"=>editions.count,
            "active_keys"=>DatasetRow.where(dataset_stream_id: stream.id, status: "active").count,
            "removed_keys"=>DatasetRow.where(dataset_stream_id: stream.id, status: "removed").count})
          return 0
        end
        importer = DatasetExample.importer(stream: stream, tenant_key: options[:tenant],
          delivery_directory: options[:delivery], manifest_sha256: options[:manifest], mapping_path: options[:mapping])
        case command
        when "preview"
          directory = Files.directory(options[:out])
          preview = importer.preview
          begin
            stem = "preview-#{preview.sha256}"
            files = [
              Artifacts.write_once(File.join(directory, "#{stem}.json")) { |io| preview.write_json(io) },
              Artifacts.write_once(File.join(directory, "#{stem}.csv")) { |io| preview.write_csv(io) }
            ]
            puts RailsDataset.json(preview.summary.merge("outputs"=>files))
          ensure
            preview.close
          end
        when "commit"
          result = importer.import!(operation_key: options[:operation], expected_preview_sha256: options[:preview])
          if options[:out]
            directory = Files.directory(options[:out])
            name = "edition-#{result.fetch("revision")}-#{result.fetch("operation_sha256")}.json"
            output = Artifacts.write_once(File.join(directory,name)) do |io|
              importer.write_receipt(io, operation_key: options[:operation])
            end
            result = result.merge("complete_receipt"=>output)
          end
          puts RailsDataset.json(result)
        when "receipt"
          directory = Files.directory(options[:out])
          result = importer.receipt(operation_key: options[:operation])
          name = "edition-#{result.fetch("revision")}-#{result.fetch("operation_sha256")}.json"
          output = Artifacts.write_once(File.join(directory,name)) do |io|
            importer.write_receipt(io, operation_key: options[:operation])
          end
          puts RailsDataset.json(result.merge("complete_receipt"=>output))
        end
        0
      rescue Starforge::Error, RailsDataset::ImportError, OptionParser::ParseError => error
        warn JSON.generate({"error"=>error.respond_to?(:code) ? error.code : error.class.name,
          "details"=>error.respond_to?(:details) ? error.details : {"message"=>error.message}})
        2
      end
    end
  end
end

exit Starforge::DatasetExample::Commission.run(ARGV.dup) if File.expand_path($PROGRAM_NAME) == File.expand_path(__FILE__)

# MIT. A database job consumes one already received, complete dataset packet.
require "active_job"
require_relative "models"

module Starforge
  module DatasetExample
    class ImportDatasetJob < ActiveJob::Base
      queue_as :default

      # Resolve these paths and tenant identity on the application's server.
      # The business operation key and selected preview survive job retries.
      def perform(stream_id:, tenant_key:, delivery_directory:, manifest_sha256:,
                  mapping_path:, operation_key:, preview_sha256:, receipt_path: nil)
        stream = DatasetStream.where(tenant_key: tenant_key).find(stream_id)
        importer = DatasetExample.importer(stream: stream, tenant_key: tenant_key,
          delivery_directory: delivery_directory, manifest_sha256: manifest_sha256, mapping_path: mapping_path)
        result = importer.import!(operation_key: operation_key, expected_preview_sha256: preview_sha256)
        if receipt_path
          Artifacts.write_once(receipt_path) { |io| importer.write_receipt(io, operation_key: operation_key) }
        end
        result
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Copy these models into the same database as the original target records.
require_relative "../../rails_dataset"

module Starforge
  module DatasetExample
    class Record < ActiveRecord::Base
      self.abstract_class = true
    end

    class DatasetStream < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_streams"
      validates :tenant_key, :name, presence: true
    end

    class DatasetEdition < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_editions"
      before_update do
        if receipt_sha256_in_database.present?
          raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord, "A committed dataset edition is immutable"
        end
      end
      before_destroy { raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord, "Retain dataset edition history" }
    end

    class DatasetRow < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_rows"
      validates :status, inclusion: {in: %w[active removed]}
    end

    class DatasetEntry < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_entries"
      before_update { raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord, "A dataset entry is immutable" }
      before_destroy { raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord, "Retain dataset source rows" }
    end

    class CatalogRecord < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_catalog_records"
      validates :tenant_key, :external_id, presence: true
    end

    MODELS = {edition: DatasetEdition, row: DatasetRow, entry: DatasetEntry}.freeze

    def self.importer(stream:, tenant_key:, delivery_directory:, manifest_sha256:, mapping_path:)
      RailsDataset.need(stream.tenant_key == tenant_key, "DATASET_EXAMPLE_TENANT")
      delivery = DatasetDelivery.open(delivery_directory, expected_manifest_sha256: manifest_sha256)
      mapping = Files.parse(Files.read(mapping_path))
      RailsDataset.new(delivery: delivery, scope: CatalogRecord.where(tenant_key: tenant_key),
        stream: stream, models: MODELS, mapping: mapping)
    end

    # Stream a complete output into a new file. A retry accepts only the exact
    # original bytes; it never replaces another review or completed receipt.
    module Artifacts
      module_function
      def write_once(path)
        path = File.expand_path(path)
        directory = Files.directory(File.dirname(path))
        temp = Tempfile.new([".dataset-artifact-", ".pending"], directory)
        begin
          temp.binmode
          yield temp
          temp.flush
          temp.fsync
          count, digest = temp.size, Digest::SHA256.file(temp.path).hexdigest
          temp.close
          begin
            File.link(temp.path, path)
            Files.sync(directory)
          rescue Errno::EEXIST
            # Preview/history exports can be larger than one original data file.
            # Verify all bytes directly without imposing the native input ceiling.
            File.open(path, File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::NONBLOCK) do |file|
              before = file.stat
              Files.need(before.file? && before.size == count, "DATASET_ARTIFACT_CONFLICT")
              actual, received = Digest::SHA256.new, 0
              while (chunk = file.read(1_048_576))
                actual.update(chunk)
                received += chunk.bytesize
                Files.need(received <= count, "DATASET_ARTIFACT_CONFLICT")
              end
              after = file.stat

          end

        ensure

        end
      end
    end
  end

          Files.need(raw.end_with?(suffix) &&
            Files.hash(raw.byteslice(0,raw.bytesize-suffix.bytesize) + "}") == page["chain"] &&
            archive.is_a?(Hash) && archive["schema"] == "stellar-forge.buyer-page-archive.v1" &&
            %w[schema index previous intent requestCursor sourceSha256 evidenceSha256 signature chain].all? {
              |key| archive[key] == page[key]
            }, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_ARCHIVE_CHANGED")
          payload = archive["payload"]
          Files.need(payload.is_a?(Hash) && payload["schema"] == "stellar-forge.dataset-page.v1" &&
            payload["fields"] == fields && payload.dig("dataset","snapshot") == snapshot &&
            payload.dig("dataset","name") == scan["name"] && payload["rows"].is_a?(Array) &&
            payload["rows"].length == page["returned"] &&
            payload.dig("page","returned") == page["returned"] && payload.dig("page","total") == row_count,
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_ARCHIVE_ROWS_CHANGED")
          columns = payload.dig("dataset","columns")
          Files.need(columns.is_a?(Array) && columns.all? { |column| column.is_a?(Hash) } &&
            fields.map { |name| columns.find { |column| column["name"] == name } } == @native_receipt["columns"] &&
            payload["semantics"] == @semantics, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_PAGE_MEANING_CHANGED")
          payload["rows"].each do |original|
            line = rows.gets("\n",2_097_153)
            Files.need(line && line.end_with?("\n") && line.bytesize <= 2_097_152 &&
              same_typed_value?(Files.parse(line,decimals: true),original),
              "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_JSONL_SOURCE_CHANGED")
            count += 1

          cursor = payload.dig("page","nextCursor")
          Files.need(count <= row_count && (index == scan["pages"].length-1 ? cursor.nil? : cursor.is_a?(String)),
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_PAGE_RANGE_CHANGED")
          if cursor
            Files.need(/\A[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,512}\z/.match?(cursor), "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_CURSOR_CHANGED")
            decoded = Base64.urlsafe_decode64(cursor)

              Files.parse(decoded) == {"v"=>1,"s"=>snapshot,"q"=>scan["queryHash"],"n"=>count},
              "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_CURSOR_CHANGED")
          end
          previous = page["chain"]
          intents[page["intent"]] = true
          source_hashes[page["sourceSha256"]] = true
        end
        Files.need(rows.read(1).nil? && count == row_count && cursor.nil? && previous == scan["chain"],
          "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_COMPLETE_ROWS_REQUIRED")
      end
    end
  end

    def self.selected_request(directory)
      root = Files.directory(directory)

        HASH.match?(request["nativeManifestSha256"].to_s), "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_REQUEST_INVALID")
      [root,request,bytes]
    end

    # A completed business operation opens from its own received bytes. Neither
    # the original room nor the original runtime has to remain mounted.
    def self.received(directory:, expected_manifest_sha256: nil)
      root,request,bytes = selected_request(directory)
      receipt = Files.parse(Files.read(File.join(root,"received.json"),1_048_576))
      Files.need(receipt.is_a?(Hash) && receipt["schema"] == RESULT_SCHEMA &&
        receipt["requestSha256"] == Files.hash(bytes) && receipt["datasetId"] == request["datasetId"] &&

        receipt["directory"] == File.join(root,"received") &&
        HASH.match?(receipt["manifestSha256"].to_s) &&
        (expected_manifest_sha256.nil? || expected_manifest_sha256 == receipt["manifestSha256"]),
        "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_BUSINESS_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
      delivery = DatasetDelivery.open(receipt["directory"],expected_manifest_sha256: receipt["manifestSha256"])

        delivery.file_bytes("selection.json",limit: 1_048_576) == bytes &&
        delivery.manifest["datasetId"] == request["datasetId"] &&
        delivery.manifest["sourceKey"] == request["sourceKey"] &&
        delivery.source_sha256 == request["nativeManifestSha256"] &&

    def self.resume(directory:, cancel: nil, timeout: 1800)
      root,request,_bytes = selected_request(directory)

      receiver = allocate

    end

    def self.status(directory:)
      root,request,bytes = selected_request(directory)

        delivery = received(directory: root)

          "requestSha256"=>Files.hash(bytes),"datasetId"=>request["datasetId"],"sourceKey"=>request["sourceKey"],
          "delivery"=>delivery.directory,"manifestSha256"=>delivery.manifest_sha256,
          "sourceId"=>delivery.source_sha256,"rowCount"=>delivery.row_count,"fields"=>delivery.fields,
          "membership"=>delivery.membership,"files"=>delivery.manifest["files"]}

        "NATIVE_RECEIVED" : "PREPARED","directory"=>root,"requestSha256"=>Files.hash(bytes),

        root = Files.directory(File.join(checkout,relative),private: false)
        Dir.children(root).sort.each do |name|
          paths << relative+"/"+name if name.end_with?(suffix) && /\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\z/.match?(name)
        end
      end
      files = paths.uniq.sort.map do |name|
        raw = Files.read(File.join(checkout,name))
        {"name"=>name,"bytes"=>raw.bytesize,"sha256"=>Files.hash(raw)}
      end
      {"directory"=>checkout,"python"=>executable(python),"node"=>executable(node),"files"=>files}
    end

    def initialize(directory:, room:, source_key:, dataset_id:, expected_native_manifest_sha256:,
      checkout:, python:, node:)
      Files.need(INTENT.match?(source_key.to_s) && INTENT.match?(dataset_id.to_s) &&
        HASH.match?(expected_native_manifest_sha256.to_s), "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SELECTION_REQUIRED")
      selected_directory = File.expand_path(directory)
      if File.exist?(File.join(selected_directory,"request.json"))
        root,original,raw = self.class.selected_request(selected_directory)
        Files.lock(root) do
          runtime = original["runtime"]
          legacy = original["runtimePathMode"].nil?
          Files.need(original["room"] == File.expand_path(room) &&
            original["sourceKey"] == source_key && original["datasetId"] == dataset_id &&
            original["nativeManifestSha256"] == expected_native_manifest_sha256 &&
            runtime.is_a?(Hash) && runtime["directory"] == File.expand_path(checkout) &&
            self.class.matches_executable?(python,runtime["python"],legacy: legacy) &&
            self.class.matches_executable?(node,runtime["node"],legacy: legacy) &&
            Files.read(File.join(root,"request.json"),1_048_576) == raw,
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_ORIGINAL_REQUEST_CHANGED")
          initialize_retained(root,original,raw)
        end
        return
      end
      @room = Files.directory(room)
      Files.directory(File.join(@room,"pages"))
      original = Files.read(File.join(@room,"manifest.json"),4_194_304)
      Files.need(Files.hash(original) == expected_native_manifest_sha256, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SOURCE_MANIFEST_CHANGED")
      @runtime = self.class.runtime_binding(checkout,python,node)
      @request = {"schema"=>NativeDatasetDelivery::SELECTION_SCHEMA,"sourceFormat"=>"SF100_SCAN",
        "sourceKey"=>source_key,"datasetId"=>dataset_id,"room"=>@room,
        "nativeManifestSha256"=>expected_native_manifest_sha256,"runtime"=>@runtime,
        "runtimePathMode"=>"selected-absolute"}
      @request_bytes = Files.json(@request).freeze
      Files.need(@request_bytes.bytesize <= 1_048_576, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_RUNTIME_SELECTION_LIMIT")
      @request_sha256 = Files.hash(@request_bytes).freeze
      @directory = Files.directory(directory,create: true)
      Files.need(@directory != @room && !@directory.start_with?(@room+File::SEPARATOR) &&
        !@room.start_with?(@directory+File::SEPARATOR), "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SEPARATE_RECEIVING_DIRECTORY_REQUIRED")
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        Files.once(File.join(@directory,"request.json"),@request_bytes)
        Files.directory(File.join(@directory,"attempts"),create: true)
        Files.directory(File.join(@directory,"received"),create: true)
      end
      DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@request)
      DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@runtime)
    end

    def same_request!
      Files.need(Files.read(File.join(@directory,"request.json"),1_048_576) == @request_bytes,
        "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_REQUEST_CHANGED")
    end

    def receive(cancel: nil, timeout: 1800)
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        same_request!
        return self.class.received(directory: @directory) if File.exist?(File.join(@directory,"received.json"))
        receipt_path = File.join(@directory,"native-receiving.json")
        unless File.exist?(receipt_path)
          Files.need(self.class.runtime_binding(@runtime["directory"],@runtime["python"],@runtime["node"]) == @runtime,
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_RUNTIME_CHANGED")
          Files.need(Files.hash(Files.read(File.join(@room,"manifest.json"),4_194_304)) ==
            @request["nativeManifestSha256"], "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SOURCE_MANIFEST_CHANGED")
          attempt = Files.directory(File.join(@directory,"attempts",SecureRandom.uuid),create: true)
          Files.once(File.join(attempt,"attempt.json"),Files.json({"schema"=>"stellar-forge.ruby-native-dataset-read.v1",
            "requestSha256"=>@request_sha256,"startedAt"=>Time.now.utc.iso8601(6)}))
          environment = {"LANG"=>"C.UTF-8","LC_ALL"=>"C.UTF-8","TZ"=>"UTC"}
          run = Runner.new(node: @runtime["python"],environment: environment).run(
            File.join(@runtime["directory"],ENTRY),
            ["--room",@room,"--node",@runtime["node"]],interpreter_arguments: ["-I","-B"],
            process_group: true,timeout: timeout,limit: 16_777_216,cancel: cancel)
          Files.once(File.join(attempt,"stdout.json"),run[:stdout])
          Files.once(File.join(attempt,"stderr.json"),run[:stderr])
          Files.once(File.join(attempt,"result.json"),Files.json({
            "schema"=>"stellar-forge.ruby-native-dataset-read-result.v1","requestSha256"=>@request_sha256,
            "exitStatus"=>run[:status].exitstatus,"termSignal"=>run[:status].termsig,"error"=>run[:error],
            "stdout"=>{"bytes"=>run[:stdout].bytesize,"sha256"=>Files.hash(run[:stdout])},
            "stderr"=>{"bytes"=>run[:stderr].bytesize,"sha256"=>Files.hash(run[:stderr])},
            "finishedAt"=>Time.now.utc.iso8601(6)}))
          raise Error, run[:error] if run[:error]
          unless run[:status].success?
            native_error = begin
              parsed = Files.parse(run[:stderr])
              parsed.is_a?(Hash) && /\A[A-Z0-9_]{1,120}\z/.match?(parsed["error"].to_s) ? parsed["error"] : nil
            rescue Error
              nil
            end
            raise Error, native_error || "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_RECEIVING_FAILED"
          end
          Files.need(self.class.runtime_binding(@runtime["directory"],@runtime["python"],@runtime["node"]) == @runtime,
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_RUNTIME_CHANGED")
          NativeDatasetDelivery.check_receipt(Files.parse(run[:stdout],decimals: true),
            room: @room,manifest_sha256: @request["nativeManifestSha256"])
          same_request!
          Files.once(receipt_path,run[:stdout])
        end
        raw = Files.read(receipt_path,16_777_216)
        receipt = Files.parse(raw,decimals: true)
        output_names,archive_names = NativeDatasetDelivery.check_receipt(receipt,
          room: @room,manifest_sha256: @request["nativeManifestSha256"])
        native = receipt.fetch("native")
        target = Files.directory(File.join(@directory,"received"))
        files = []
        (output_names+archive_names).each do |name|
          raise Error, "RUBY_NATIVE_CANCELLED" if cancel&.cancelled?
          original = native["outputs"][name] || native["archives"][name]
          descriptor = {"name"=>name,"bytes"=>original["bytes"],"sha256"=>original["sha256"]}
          copy_original(target,name,descriptor)
          files << descriptor
        end
        dictionary = files.find { |item| item["name"] == "semantics.json" }
        semantics = if dictionary
          DatasetDelivery.snapshot_file(File.join(target,"semantics.json"),dictionary) do |stream|
            Files.parse(stream.read,decimals: true)
          end
        end
        source = {"schema"=>NativeDatasetDelivery::SOURCE_SCHEMA,"sourceFormat"=>"SF100_SCAN",
          "sourceKey"=>@request["sourceKey"],"datasetId"=>@request["datasetId"],"originalRoom"=>@room,
          "sourceId"=>receipt["sourceId"],"manifestSha256"=>receipt["manifestSha256"],
          "sourceBindingSha256"=>receipt["sourceBindingSha256"],
          "datasetName"=>native["originalNativeScan"]["name"],"columns"=>receipt["columns"],
          "providerIdentity"=>NativeDatasetDelivery.provider_identity(semantics),"semanticsFile"=>dictionary}
        metadata = {"selection.json"=>@request_bytes,"native-receiving.json"=>raw,"source.json"=>Files.json(source)}
        metadata.each do |name,bytes|
          NativeDatasetDelivery.check_descriptor(name,{"bytes"=>bytes.bytesize,"sha256"=>Files.hash(bytes)})
          Files.once(File.join(target,name),bytes)
          files << {"name"=>name,"bytes"=>bytes.bytesize,"sha256"=>Files.hash(bytes)}
        end
        scan = native.fetch("originalNativeScan")
        manifest = {"schema"=>NativeDatasetDelivery::SCHEMA,"sourceFormat"=>"SF100_SCAN",
          "sourceKey"=>@request["sourceKey"],"datasetId"=>@request["datasetId"],
          "sourceSha256"=>receipt["sourceId"],"nativeManifestSha256"=>receipt["manifestSha256"],
          "sourceBindingSha256"=>receipt["sourceBindingSha256"],"nativeReceiptSha256"=>Files.hash(raw),
          "sourceRecordSha256"=>Files.hash(metadata["source.json"]),"selectionSha256"=>@request_sha256,
          "snapshot"=>scan["snapshot"],"rowCount"=>scan["count"],"fields"=>scan["fields"],"files"=>files}
        bytes = Files.json(manifest)
        same_request!
        Files.once(File.join(target,DatasetDelivery::MANIFEST),bytes)
        delivery = DatasetDelivery.open(target,expected_manifest_sha256: Files.hash(bytes))
        completion = {"schema"=>RESULT_SCHEMA,"requestSha256"=>@request_sha256,
          "datasetId"=>@request["datasetId"],"sourceKey"=>@request["sourceKey"],
          "sourceId"=>receipt["sourceId"],"nativeReceiptSha256"=>Files.hash(raw),
          "directory"=>target,"manifestSha256"=>delivery.manifest_sha256}
        Files.once(File.join(@directory,"received.json"),Files.json(completion))
        self.class.received(directory: @directory)
      end
    end

    private
    def initialize_retained(root, request, bytes)
      runtime = request["runtime"]
      Files.need(request["room"].is_a?(String) && File.expand_path(request["room"]) == request["room"] &&
        runtime.is_a?(Hash) && runtime["files"].is_a?(Array) &&
        %w[directory python node].all? { |key| runtime[key].is_a?(String) &&
          File.expand_path(runtime[key]) == runtime[key] }, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_RUNTIME_SELECTION_INVALID")
      @directory,@request,@request_bytes = root,request,bytes.dup.freeze
      @room,@runtime,@request_sha256 = request["room"],runtime,Files.hash(bytes).freeze
      DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@request)
      Files.directory(File.join(root,"attempts"),create: true)
      Files.directory(File.join(root,"received"),create: true)
    end

    def copy_original(target, name, expected)
      parent = DatasetDelivery.parent_directory(target,name,create: true)
      destination = File.join(parent,File.basename(name))
      if File.exist?(destination) || File.symlink?(destination)
        DatasetDelivery.snapshot_file(destination,expected) { |_stream| }
        return
      end
      # The same descriptor is fully verified before any bytes enter the packet.
      # Atomic create-only publication lets an interrupted transfer resume.
      DatasetDelivery.parent_directory(@room,name)
      temp = Tempfile.new([".native-dataset-", ".pending"],parent)
      begin
        temp.binmode
        DatasetDelivery.snapshot_file(File.join(@room,name),expected) do |source|
          while (chunk = source.read(1_048_576))
            written = 0
            while written < chunk.bytesize
              count = temp.write(chunk.byteslice(written,chunk.bytesize-written))
              Files.need(count && count > 0, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_COPY_FAILED")
              written += count
            end
          end
        end
        temp.flush
        temp.fsync
        temp.close
        begin
          File.link(temp.path,destination)
          Files.sync(parent)
        rescue Errno::EEXIST
          DatasetDelivery.snapshot_file(destination,expected) { |_stream| }
        end
      ensure
        temp.close!
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Complete dataset revision import into the customer's original Rails database.
require "active_record"
require "active_support/time"
require "set"
require "date"
require "time"
require "csv"
require_relative "dataset_delivery"

module Starforge
  class RailsDataset
    SCHEMA = "stellar-forge.rails-dataset-import.v1"
    TYPES = %w[string integer decimal boolean date datetime].freeze

    class ImportError < StandardError
      attr_reader :code, :details
      def initialize(code, **details)
        @code, @details = code, details
        super([code, details.map { |key,value| "#{key}=#{value.inspect}" }.join(" ")].reject(&:empty?).join(": "))
      end
    end

    def self.need(condition, code, **details)
      raise ImportError.new(code, **details) unless condition
    end

    # Tagged values preserve native integers, decimal precision and dates in
    # complete previews/receipts without JSON's binary-number conversions.
    def self.pack(value)
      case value
      when NilClass then ["null"]
      when TrueClass, FalseClass then ["boolean", value]
      when String then ["string", value]
      when Integer then ["integer", value.to_s]
      when BigDecimal
        need(value.finite?, "DATASET_FINITE_DECIMAL")
        ["decimal", value.to_s("F")]
      when ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, Time, DateTime then ["datetime", value.to_time.utc.iso8601(9)]
      when Date then ["date", value.iso8601]
      when Array then ["array", value.map { |item| pack(item) }]
      when Hash
        need(value.keys.all? { |key| key.is_a?(String) }, "DATASET_STRING_KEYS")
        ["object", value.keys.sort.map { |key| [key, pack(value.fetch(key))] }]
      else
        raise ImportError.new("DATASET_EXACT_VALUE", type: value.class.name)
      end
    end

    def self.unpack(value)
      type, data = value
      case type
      when "null" then nil
      when "boolean", "string" then data
      when "integer" then Integer(data, 10)
      when "decimal" then BigDecimal(data)
      when "date" then Date.iso8601(data)
      when "datetime" then Time.iso8601(data)
      when "array" then data.map { |item| unpack(item) }
      when "object" then data.to_h { |key,item| [key, unpack(item)] }
      else raise ImportError.new("DATASET_TAGGED_VALUE")
      end
    end

    def self.json(value)
      JSON.generate(value, allow_nan: false, max_nesting: 100)
    end

    def self.exact_json(value)
      json(pack(value))
    end

    def self.sha(value)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(value.b)
    end

    def self.fingerprint(value)
      sha(exact_json(value))
    end

    def self.copy_json(value)
      JSON.parse(json(value), create_additions: false, allow_nan: false)
    end

    # The complete original source is streamed into a private preview, then
    # streamed again when reviewed or committed. Only key identities stay in RAM.
    class Preview
      attr_reader :binding, :counts, :sha256, :entries_sha256, :row_count
      def initialize(binding)
        @binding = RailsDataset.copy_json(binding)
        @counts = {"inserted"=>0, "updated"=>0, "unchanged"=>0, "removed"=>0,
                   "adopted"=>0, "restored"=>0, "source_changed"=>0}
        @file = Tempfile.new(["starforge-dataset-preview-", ".jsonl"])
        @file.binmode
        @file.unlink
        @digest, @row_count, @sealed, @closed = Digest::SHA256.new, 0, false, false
      end

      def append(entry)
        RailsDataset.need(!@sealed && !@closed, "DATASET_PREVIEW_SEALED")
        raw = RailsDataset.json(entry) + "\n"
        @file.write(raw)
        @digest.update(raw)
        @row_count += 1
        @counts.fetch(entry.fetch("action"))
        @counts[entry.fetch("action")] += 1
        %w[adopted restored source_changed].each { |key| @counts[key] += 1 if entry[key] }
      end

      def seal
        RailsDataset.need(!@closed, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CLOSED")
        unless @sealed
          @file.flush
          @entries_sha256 = @digest.hexdigest
          @sha256 = RailsDataset.fingerprint({"schema"=>SCHEMA, "binding"=>@binding,
            "counts"=>@counts, "row_count"=>@row_count, "entries_sha256"=>@entries_sha256})
          DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@binding)
          DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@counts)
          @sha256.freeze
          @entries_sha256.freeze
          @sealed = true
        end
        self
      end

      def each_entry
        return enum_for(__method__) unless block_given?
        RailsDataset.need(@sealed && !@closed, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CLOSED")
        @file.rewind
        seen = Digest::SHA256.new
        @file.each_line do |line|
          seen.update(line)
          yield JSON.parse(line, create_additions: false, allow_nan: false)
        end
        RailsDataset.need(seen.hexdigest == @entries_sha256, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CHANGED")
        self
      end

      def summary
        RailsDataset.need(@sealed && !@closed, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CLOSED")
        {"schema"=>SCHEMA, "binding"=>RailsDataset.copy_json(@binding),
         "preview_sha256"=>@sha256, "entries_sha256"=>@entries_sha256,
         "row_count"=>@row_count, "counts"=>@counts.dup}
      end

      def write_json(io)
        header = RailsDataset.json(summary)
        io.write(header.delete_suffix("}") + ',"rows":[')
        first = true
        each_entry do |row|
          io.write(",") unless first
          io.write(RailsDataset.json(row))
          first = false
        end
        io.write("]}\n")
        self
      end

      def write_csv(io)
        csv = CSV.new(io, force_quotes: true, row_sep: "\n")
        csv << %w[action source_ordinal key target_id adopted restored source_changed before after original_source_json source_row_sha256]
        each_entry do |row|
          csv << [row["action"], row["source_ordinal"], row["key_json"], row["target_id"],
            row["adopted"], row["restored"], row["source_changed"],
            row["before_json"], row["after_json"], row["source_raw_json"], row["source_row_sha256"]]
        end
        csv.flush
        self
      end

      def close
        return if @closed
        @closed = true
        @file.close
      end
    end

    # Explicit field mapping; a missing field can be preserved, while a supplied
    # null can independently be assigned or preserved. Keys always need values.
    class Mapping
      attr_reader :definition, :columns, :key_columns, :sha256, :key_sha256, :removal
      def initialize(definition, model, fields, protected_columns)
        RailsDataset.need(definition.is_a?(Hash), "DATASET_MAPPING")
        @definition = RailsDataset.copy_json(definition)
        RailsDataset.need(@definition["schema"] == "stellar-forge.rails-dataset-mapping.v1",
          "DATASET_MAPPING_SCHEMA")
        @columns, @key_columns = @definition["columns"], @definition["key_columns"]
        RailsDataset.need(@columns.is_a?(Hash) && !@columns.empty? &&
          @key_columns.is_a?(Array) && !@key_columns.empty? &&
          @key_columns.uniq == @key_columns && @key_columns.all? { |key| key.is_a?(String) && @columns.key?(key) },
          "DATASET_MAPPING_KEYS")
        @model = model
        @columns.each do |name,spec|
          RailsDataset.need(name.is_a?(String) && model.columns_hash.key?(name) &&
            !protected_columns.include?(name), "DATASET_TARGET_COLUMN", column: name)
          RailsDataset.need(spec.is_a?(Hash) && fields.include?(spec["field"]) &&
            TYPES.include?(spec["type"]) && %w[assign preserve].include?(spec.fetch("null", "assign")) &&
            %w[error preserve].include?(spec.fetch("missing", "error")) &&
            [true,false].include?(spec.fetch("stringify", false)), "DATASET_FIELD_MAPPING", column: name)
          RailsDataset.need((spec.keys - %w[field type null missing stringify]).empty?,
            "DATASET_MAPPING_OPTION", column: name)
          RailsDataset.need(!@key_columns.include?(name) ||
            (spec.fetch("null", "assign") == "assign" && spec.fetch("missing", "error") == "error"),
            "DATASET_KEY_REQUIRED", column: name)
          verify_type(name, spec["type"])
        end
        @removal = @definition.fetch("removal", {"strategy"=>"retain"})
        RailsDataset.need(@removal.is_a?(Hash) && %w[retain archive].include?(@removal["strategy"]),
          "DATASET_REMOVAL_POLICY")
        allowed_removal = @removal["strategy"] == "archive" ? %w[strategy column active inactive] : %w[strategy]
        RailsDataset.need((@removal.keys - allowed_removal).empty?, "DATASET_REMOVAL_OPTION")
        if @removal["strategy"] == "archive"
          name = @removal["column"]
          RailsDataset.need(name.is_a?(String) && model.columns_hash.key?(name) &&
            model.type_for_attribute(name).type == :boolean &&
            !protected_columns.include?(name) && !@columns.key?(name),
            "DATASET_ARCHIVE_COLUMN")
          RailsDataset.need(@removal.fetch("active", true) == true && @removal.fetch("inactive", false) == false,
            "DATASET_ARCHIVE_BOOLEAN")
        end
        RailsDataset.need((@definition.keys - %w[schema columns key_columns removal]).empty?,
          "DATASET_MAPPING_OPTION")
        DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@definition)
        DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@removal)
        @sha256 = RailsDataset.fingerprint(@definition).freeze
        @key_sha256 = RailsDataset.fingerprint({"key_columns"=>@key_columns,
          "columns"=>@columns.slice(*@key_columns)}).freeze
      end

      def verify_type(name, type)
        actual = @model.type_for_attribute(name).type
        accepted = {"string"=>[:string,:text], "integer"=>[:integer],
          "decimal"=>[:decimal], "boolean"=>[:boolean], "date"=>[:date],
          "datetime"=>[:datetime,:timestamp]}
        RailsDataset.need(accepted.fetch(type).include?(actual), "DATASET_COLUMN_TYPE",
          column: name, declared: type, actual: actual)
      end

      def converted(name, spec, value)
        if value.nil?
          RailsDataset.need(@model.columns_hash.fetch(name).null, "DATASET_COLUMN_NULL", column: name)
          return nil
        end
        selected = case spec["type"]
        when "string"
          if value.is_a?(String)
            value
          elsif spec["stringify"] && (value.is_a?(Integer) || value.is_a?(BigDecimal) || value == true || value == false)
            value.is_a?(BigDecimal) ? value.to_s("F") : value.to_s
          else
            raise ImportError.new("DATASET_TEXT_REQUIRED", column: name)
          end
        when "integer"
          if value.is_a?(Integer)
            value
          elsif value.is_a?(BigDecimal) && value.finite? && value.frac.zero?
            value.to_i
          elsif value.is_a?(String) && /\A[+-]?[0-9]+\z/.match?(value)
            Integer(value, 10)
          else
            raise ImportError.new("DATASET_INTEGER_REQUIRED", column: name)
          end
        when "decimal"
          RailsDataset.need(value.is_a?(Integer) || value.is_a?(BigDecimal) ||
            value.is_a?(String) && /\A[+-]?(?:[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]*)?|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?\z/.match?(value),
            "DATASET_DECIMAL_REQUIRED", column: name)
          parsed = value.is_a?(BigDecimal) ? value : BigDecimal(value.to_s)
          RailsDataset.need(parsed.finite?, "DATASET_FINITE_DECIMAL", column: name)
          parsed
        when "boolean"
          RailsDataset.need(value == true || value == false, "DATASET_BOOLEAN_REQUIRED", column: name)
          value
        when "date"
          RailsDataset.need(value.is_a?(String) && /\A[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\z/.match?(value),
            "DATASET_DATE_REQUIRED", column: name)
          Date.iso8601(value)
        when "datetime"
          RailsDataset.need(value.is_a?(String) &&
            /\A[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T.+(?:Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})\z/.match?(value),
            "DATASET_TIMESTAMP_OFFSET", column: name)
          Time.iso8601(value).utc
        end
        if selected.is_a?(String)
          RailsDataset.need(selected.valid_encoding? && !selected.include?("\0"), "DATASET_TEXT_ENCODING", column: name)
          limit = @model.columns_hash.fetch(name).limit
          RailsDataset.need(limit.nil? || selected.length <= limit, "DATASET_TEXT_LENGTH", column: name)
        end
        if selected.is_a?(BigDecimal)
          column = @model.columns_hash.fetch(name)
          if column.precision && column.scale
            integral_digits = selected.zero? ? 0 : [selected.abs.exponent, 0].max
            RailsDataset.need(integral_digits <= column.precision - column.scale,
              "DATASET_DECIMAL_RANGE", column: name, precision: column.precision, scale: column.scale)
          end
        end
        type = @model.type_for_attribute(name)
        returned = type.deserialize(type.serialize(selected))
        RailsDataset.need(returned == selected, "DATASET_COLUMN_PRECISION", column: name,
          selected: selected.to_s, stored: returned.to_s)
        selected
      rescue ArgumentError, RangeError => error
        raise ImportError.new("DATASET_COLUMN_VALUE", column: name, reason: error.message)
      end

      def values(row)
        RailsDataset.need(row.is_a?(Hash), "DATASET_SOURCE_ROW")
        result = {}
        @columns.each do |name,spec|
          field = spec.fetch("field")
          unless row.key?(field)
            RailsDataset.need(spec.fetch("missing", "error") == "preserve",
              "DATASET_SOURCE_FIELD_MISSING", field: field)
            next
          end
          next if row[field].nil? && spec.fetch("null", "assign") == "preserve"
          result[name] = converted(name, spec, row[field])
        end
        @key_columns.each do |name|
          value = result[name]
          RailsDataset.need(!value.nil? && !(value.is_a?(String) && value.empty?),
            "DATASET_KEY_REQUIRED", column: name)
        end
        result[@removal["column"]] = true if @removal["strategy"] == "archive"
        result
      end

      def key(values)
        selected = @key_columns.to_h { |name| [name, values.fetch(name)] }
        raw = RailsDataset.exact_json(selected)
        [RailsDataset.sha(raw), raw]
      end

      def removed_values
        @removal["strategy"] == "archive" ? {@removal.fetch("column")=>false} : {}
      end

      def target_columns
        (@columns.keys + (@removal["strategy"] == "archive" ? [@removal["column"]] : [])).uniq
      end
    end

    attr_reader :mapping

    # models contains the application's edition, row and entry ActiveRecord
    # classes. stream is its persisted stream record; scope is its authorized
    # tenant relation. Every model must use the very same database connection.
    def initialize(delivery:, scope:, stream:, models:, mapping:)
      self.class.need(delivery.is_a?(DatasetDelivery), "DATASET_ORIGINAL_DELIVERY")
      self.class.need(scope.is_a?(ActiveRecord::Relation) && stream.is_a?(ActiveRecord::Base) &&
        stream.persisted?, "DATASET_NATIVE_SCOPE")
      self.class.need(models.is_a?(Hash) && %i[edition row entry].all? { |key|
        models[key].is_a?(Class) && models[key] < ActiveRecord::Base }, "DATASET_NATIVE_MODELS")
      @delivery, @scope, @stream = delivery, scope.reorder(nil), stream
      @model, @models = @scope.klass, models.slice(:edition, :row, :entry).freeze
      self.class.need(@scope.limit_value.nil? && @scope.offset_value.nil? &&
        @scope.group_values.empty?, "DATASET_COMPLETE_TARGET_SCOPE")
      pool = @stream.class.connection_pool
      self.class.need(([@model] + @models.values).all? { |model| model.connection_pool.equal?(pool) },
        "DATASET_ONE_DATABASE")
      self.class.need(@model.primary_key.is_a?(String), "DATASET_TARGET_PRIMARY_KEY")
      @pk = @model.primary_key
      @scope_values = @scope.scope_for_create.stringify_keys
      protected_columns = ([@pk, @model.inheritance_column, "created_at", "updated_at", "lock_version"] +
        @scope_values.keys).compact.uniq
      @mapping = Mapping.new(mapping, @model, @delivery.fields, protected_columns)
      @scope_sha = self.class.fingerprint({"model"=>@model.name, "sql"=>@scope.to_sql,
        "creation_values"=>@scope_values})
      @membership = self.class.copy_json(@delivery.membership)
      self.class.need(@membership.is_a?(Hash) &&
        @membership["query_sha256"].is_a?(String) &&
        /\A[a-f0-9]{64}\z/.match?(@membership["query_sha256"]) &&
        @membership["projected_fields"] == @delivery.fields, "DATASET_QUERY_MEMBERSHIP")
      DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@membership)
      @membership_sha = self.class.fingerprint(@membership)
      @schema_sha = self.class.fingerprint(@mapping.target_columns.sort.map do |name|
        column = @model.columns_hash.fetch(name)
        {"name"=>name, "type"=>column.type.to_s, "sql_type"=>column.sql_type,
         "limit"=>column.limit, "precision"=>column.precision, "scale"=>column.scale, "null"=>column.null}
      end)
      verify_unique_key!
    end

    def verify_unique_key!
      allowed = (@mapping.key_columns + @scope_values.keys).uniq
      indexes = @model.connection.indexes(@model.table_name)
      eligible = indexes.any? do |index|
        columns = index.columns
        index.unique && columns.is_a?(Array) &&
          (@mapping.key_columns - columns).empty? && (columns - allowed).empty? &&
          (!index.respond_to?(:where) || index.where.nil? || index.where.empty?)
      end
      self.class.need(eligible, "DATASET_UNIQUE_TARGET_KEY",
        columns: @mapping.key_columns, scope_columns: @scope_values.keys)
    end

    def validate_stream!
      {"target_model"=>@model.name, "scope_sha256"=>@scope_sha,
       "key_mapping_sha256"=>@mapping.key_sha256, "membership_sha256"=>@membership_sha}.each do |key,expected|
        actual = @stream.public_send(key)
        self.class.need(actual.nil? || actual == expected, "DATASET_STREAM_BINDING", field: key)
      end
      self.class.need(@stream.revision.is_a?(Integer) && @stream.revision >= 0, "DATASET_STREAM_REVISION")
    end

    def source_binding
      {"manifest_sha256"=>@delivery.manifest_sha256, "source_sha256"=>@delivery.source_sha256,
       "snapshot"=>self.class.pack(@delivery.snapshot), "row_count"=>@delivery.row_count,
       "fields"=>@delivery.fields, "membership"=>@membership}
    end

    def prior_receipt
      return nil if @stream.latest_edition_id.nil?
      edition = @models[:edition].find_by(id: @stream.latest_edition_id, dataset_stream_id: @stream.id)
      self.class.need(edition, "DATASET_PRIOR_EDITION_MISSING")
      verified_receipt(edition)
      self.class.need(edition.revision == @stream.revision, "DATASET_PRIOR_REVISION_CHANGED")
      edition.receipt_sha256
    end

    def binding
      validate_stream!
      {"stream_id"=>@stream.id.to_s, "target_model"=>@model.name, "scope_sha256"=>@scope_sha,
       "source"=>source_binding, "mapping"=>@mapping.definition, "mapping_sha256"=>@mapping.sha256,
       "schema_sha256"=>@schema_sha, "prior_revision"=>@stream.revision,
       "prior_edition_id"=>@stream.latest_edition_id&.to_s, "prior_receipt_sha256"=>prior_receipt}
    end

    def preview
      result = nil
      @stream.with_lock { result = build_preview }
      result
    end

    def key_tuple(record)
      @mapping.key_columns.to_h { |name| [name, record.public_send(name)] }
    end

    def target_values(record, columns)
      return {} unless record
      columns.to_h { |name| [name, record.public_send(name)] }
    end

    def target_fingerprint(record, columns)
      values = {"present"=>!record.nil?, "id"=>record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s,
        "values"=>target_values(record, columns)}
      values["lock_version"] = record.lock_version if record && record.has_attribute?("lock_version")
      self.class.fingerprint(values)
    end

    def matching_targets(batch)
      table = @model.arel_table
      predicates = batch.map do |row|
        @mapping.key_columns.map { |name| table[name].eq(row.fetch("values").fetch(name)) }.reduce(&:and)
      end
      return {} if predicates.empty?
      @scope.where(predicates.reduce(&:or)).lock.to_a.group_by do |record|
        @mapping.key(key_tuple(record)).first
      end
    end

    def append_incoming(plan, batch, seen_targets)
      states = @models[:row].where(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id,
        key_sha256: batch.map { |row| row["key_sha256"] }).to_a.index_by(&:key_sha256)
      ids = states.values.map(&:target_id).compact
      tracked = ids.empty? ? {} : @scope.where(@pk=>ids).lock.to_a.index_by { |record| record.public_send(@pk).to_s }
      missing_ids = ids.map(&:to_s) - tracked.keys
      if !missing_ids.empty? && @model.unscoped.where(@pk=>missing_ids).exists?
        raise ImportError.new("DATASET_MANAGED_TARGET_OUTSIDE_SCOPE")
      end
      candidates = matching_targets(batch)
      selected = batch.map do |row|
        state = states[row["key_sha256"]]
        original = state && tracked[state.target_id.to_s]
        found = candidates.fetch(row["key_sha256"], [])
        found = ([original] + found).compact.uniq { |record| record.public_send(@pk).to_s }
        self.class.need(found.length <= 1, "DATASET_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS", key: row["key_json"])
        [row, state, found.first]
      end
      target_ids = selected.map { |_,_,record| record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s }.compact
      owners = @models[:row].where(target_model: @model.name, target_id: target_ids).to_a
        .index_by { |row| row.target_id.to_s }
      selected.each do |row,state,record|
        target_id = record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s
        if target_id
          self.class.need(seen_targets.add?(target_id), "DATASET_TARGET_REUSED", target_id: target_id)
          owner = owners[target_id]
          self.class.need(owner.nil? || (owner.dataset_stream_id.to_s == @stream.id.to_s &&
            owner.key_sha256 == row["key_sha256"]), "DATASET_TARGET_ALREADY_MANAGED", target_id: target_id)
        end
        columns = row.fetch("values").keys
        before = target_values(record, columns)
        changed = !record || before != row["values"]
        action = !record ? "inserted" : changed ? "updated" : "unchanged"
        plan.append(row.except("values").merge(
          "action"=>action, "target_id"=>target_id, "state_id"=>state&.id&.to_s,
          "adopted"=>state.nil? && !record.nil?, "restored"=>state && state.status == "removed",
          "source_changed"=>state && state.source_row_sha256 != row["source_row_sha256"],
          "before_json"=>self.class.exact_json(before), "after_json"=>self.class.exact_json(row["values"]),
          "target_fingerprint"=>target_fingerprint(record, columns)))
      end
    end

    def append_removed(plan, seen_keys)
      @models[:row].where(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, status: "active").in_batches(of: 200) do |relation|
        states = relation.to_a.reject { |row| seen_keys.include?(row.key_sha256) }
        ids = states.map(&:target_id).compact
        targets = ids.empty? ? {} : @scope.where(@pk=>ids).lock.to_a.index_by { |record| record.public_send(@pk).to_s }
        states.sort_by(&:key_sha256).each do |state|
          record = targets[state.target_id.to_s]
          if record.nil? && state.target_id && @model.unscoped.where(@pk=>state.target_id).exists?
            raise ImportError.new("DATASET_MANAGED_TARGET_OUTSIDE_SCOPE")
          end
          values = @mapping.removed_values
          plan.append({"action"=>"removed", "key_sha256"=>state.key_sha256, "key_json"=>state.key_json,
            "target_id"=>record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s, "previous_target_id"=>state.target_id,
            "state_id"=>state.id.to_s, "source_ordinal"=>nil, "source_raw_json"=>nil,
            "source_row_sha256"=>nil, "adopted"=>false, "restored"=>false, "source_changed"=>false,
            "before_json"=>self.class.exact_json(target_values(record, values.keys)),
            "after_json"=>self.class.exact_json(values),
            "target_fingerprint"=>target_fingerprint(record, values.keys)})
        end
      end
    end

    def build_preview
      plan = Preview.new(binding)
      seen_keys, seen_targets, ordinal = Set.new, Set.new, 0
      # Keep SQL parameter counts practical without limiting the complete dataset.
      batch_size = [200, [800 / @mapping.key_columns.length, 1].max].min
      @delivery.each_record.each_slice(batch_size) do |records|
        selected = records.map do |record|
          self.class.need(record["ordinal"] == ordinal && record["raw_json"].is_a?(String) &&
            self.class.sha(record["raw_json"]) == record["sha256"], "DATASET_ORIGINAL_ROW", ordinal: ordinal)
          values = @mapping.values(record.fetch("values"))
          key_sha, key_json = @mapping.key(values)
          self.class.need(seen_keys.add?(key_sha), "DATASET_DUPLICATE_SOURCE_KEY", ordinal: ordinal, key: key_json)
          row = {"key_sha256"=>key_sha, "key_json"=>key_json, "values"=>values,
            "source_ordinal"=>ordinal, "source_raw_json"=>record["raw_json"], "source_row_sha256"=>record["sha256"]}
          ordinal += 1
          row
        end
        append_incoming(plan, selected, seen_targets)
      end
      self.class.need(ordinal == @delivery.row_count, "DATASET_COMPLETE_ROWS",
        actual: ordinal, declared: @delivery.row_count)
      append_removed(plan, seen_keys)
      plan.seal
    rescue Exception
      plan&.close
      raise
    end

    def verified_receipt(edition)
      raw = edition.receipt_json
      self.class.need(raw.is_a?(String) && self.class.sha(raw) == edition.receipt_sha256,
        "DATASET_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
      receipt = JSON.parse(raw, create_additions: false, allow_nan: false)
      self.class.need(receipt["schema"] == SCHEMA &&
        receipt["stream_id"] == @stream.id.to_s && receipt["edition_id"] == edition.id.to_s &&
        receipt["revision"] == edition.revision && receipt["operation_sha256"] == edition.operation_sha256 &&
        receipt["manifest_sha256"] == edition.manifest_sha256 &&
        receipt["source_sha256"] == edition.source_sha256 && receipt["mapping_sha256"] == edition.mapping_sha256 &&
        receipt["binding"] == JSON.parse(edition.binding_json) &&
        receipt["preview_sha256"] == edition.preview_sha256, "DATASET_RECEIPT_BINDING")
      receipt
    end

    def receipt(operation_key:)
      operation_sha = operation_identity(operation_key)
      edition = @models[:edition].find_by(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, operation_sha256: operation_sha)
      self.class.need(edition, "DATASET_RECEIPT_MISSING")
      validate_stream!
      verified_receipt(edition)
    end

    def operation_identity(value)
      self.class.need(value.is_a?(String) && value.valid_encoding? && !value.strip.empty? &&
        value.bytesize <= 1024, "DATASET_OPERATION_KEY")
      self.class.sha(value)
    end

    def apply_entry(entry, edition)
      values = self.class.unpack(JSON.parse(entry.fetch("after_json")))
      record = entry["target_id"] && @scope.lock.find_by(@pk=>entry["target_id"])
      self.class.need(target_fingerprint(record, values.keys) == entry["target_fingerprint"],
        "DATASET_TARGET_CHANGED", key: entry["key_json"])
      if entry["action"] == "inserted"
        record = @scope.new(values)
        self.class.need(record.save!, "DATASET_MODEL_SAVE")
      elsif record && entry["action"] != "unchanged" && !values.empty?
        record.assign_attributes(values)
        self.class.need(record.save!, "DATASET_MODEL_SAVE")
      end
      if record
        record.reload
        self.class.need(@scope.where(@pk=>record.public_send(@pk)).exists?, "DATASET_TARGET_SCOPE_CHANGED")
        self.class.need(target_values(record, values.keys) == values,
          "DATASET_STORED_VALUES_CHANGED", key: entry["key_json"])
      end
      target_id = record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s || entry["previous_target_id"]
      state = @models[:row].find_or_initialize_by(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, key_sha256: entry["key_sha256"])
      self.class.need(state.new_record? || state.id.to_s == entry["state_id"], "DATASET_KEY_STATE_CHANGED")
      state.assign_attributes(key_json: entry["key_json"], target_model: @model.name, target_id: target_id,
        status: entry["action"] == "removed" ? "removed" : "active", last_edition_id: edition.id)
      unless entry["action"] == "removed"
        state.source_row_sha256 = entry["source_row_sha256"]
        state.values_json = entry["after_json"]
      end
      expected_state = state.attributes.slice("dataset_stream_id", "key_sha256", "key_json", "target_model",
        "target_id", "status", "last_edition_id", "source_row_sha256", "values_json")
      self.class.need(state.save!, "DATASET_KEY_STATE_SAVE")
      self.class.need(state.reload.attributes.slice(*expected_state.keys) == expected_state,
        "DATASET_KEY_STATE_WRITE_CHANGED")
      stored = entry.merge("target_id"=>target_id, "edition_id"=>edition.id.to_s)
      raw = self.class.json(stored)
      @models[:entry].create!(dataset_edition_id: edition.id, key_sha256: entry["key_sha256"],
        source_ordinal: entry["source_ordinal"], action: entry["action"], target_id: target_id,
        record_json: raw, record_sha256: self.class.sha(raw))
      stored
    end

    def import!(operation_key:, expected_preview_sha256:)
      self.class.need(expected_preview_sha256.is_a?(String) &&
        /\A[a-f0-9]{64}\z/.match?(expected_preview_sha256), "DATASET_SELECTED_PREVIEW")
      self.class.need(!@stream.class.connection.transaction_open?, "DATASET_IMPORT_TRANSACTION",
        reason: "Call the importer as the job's database transaction boundary.")
      operation_sha = operation_identity(operation_key)
      result, plan = nil, nil
      @stream.with_lock do
        validate_stream!
        existing = @models[:edition].find_by(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, operation_sha256: operation_sha)
        if existing
          self.class.need(existing.manifest_sha256 == @delivery.manifest_sha256 &&
            existing.mapping_sha256 == @mapping.sha256 && existing.preview_sha256 == expected_preview_sha256,
            "DATASET_OPERATION_CHANGED")
          result = verified_receipt(existing)
        else
          plan = build_preview
          self.class.need(plan.sha256 == expected_preview_sha256, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CHANGED",
            expected: expected_preview_sha256, current: plan.sha256)
          revision = @stream.revision + 1
          edition = @models[:edition].create!(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, revision: revision,
            operation_sha256: operation_sha, manifest_sha256: @delivery.manifest_sha256,
            source_sha256: @delivery.source_sha256, mapping_sha256: @mapping.sha256,
            preview_sha256: plan.sha256, binding_json: self.class.json(plan.binding))
          retained = Digest::SHA256.new
          plan.each_entry { |entry| retained.update(self.class.json(apply_entry(entry, edition)) + "\n") }
          result = {"schema"=>SCHEMA, "stream_id"=>@stream.id.to_s, "edition_id"=>edition.id.to_s,
            "revision"=>revision, "operation_sha256"=>operation_sha,
            "manifest_sha256"=>@delivery.manifest_sha256, "source_sha256"=>@delivery.source_sha256,
            "mapping_sha256"=>@mapping.sha256, "preview_sha256"=>plan.sha256,
            "preview_entries_sha256"=>plan.entries_sha256, "retained_entries_sha256"=>retained.hexdigest,
            "binding"=>plan.binding, "counts"=>plan.counts, "entry_count"=>plan.row_count,
            "committed_at"=>Time.now.utc.iso8601(6)}
          raw = self.class.json(result)
          edition.update!(receipt_json: raw, receipt_sha256: self.class.sha(raw))
          @stream.update!(revision: revision, latest_edition_id: edition.id, target_model: @model.name,
            scope_sha256: @scope_sha, key_mapping_sha256: @mapping.key_sha256, membership_sha256: @membership_sha)
          @stream.reload
          self.class.need(@stream.revision == revision && @stream.latest_edition_id == edition.id,
            "DATASET_STREAM_WRITE_CHANGED")
          validate_stream!
          self.class.need(verified_receipt(edition.reload) == result, "DATASET_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
        end
      end
      self.class.need(result, "DATASET_IMPORT_ROLLED_BACK")
      result
    ensure
      plan&.close
    end

    # Full original edition export can be reopened independently of the current
    # source edition. Customer records and their source rows remain on the same
    # transaction history, including removed keys and exact original JSON lines.
    def write_receipt(io, operation_key:)
      operation_sha = operation_identity(operation_key)
      edition = @models[:edition].find_by(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, operation_sha256: operation_sha)
      self.class.need(edition, "DATASET_RECEIPT_MISSING")
      validate_stream!
      selected = verified_receipt(edition)
      io.write(self.class.json(selected).delete_suffix("}") + ',"rows":[')
      first, digest, count = true, Digest::SHA256.new, 0
      @models[:entry].where(dataset_edition_id: edition.id).find_each do |entry|
        raw = entry.record_json
        self.class.need(self.class.sha(raw) == entry.record_sha256, "DATASET_EDITION_ROW_CHANGED")
        digest.update(raw + "\n")
        io.write(",") unless first
        io.write(raw)
        first = false
        count += 1
      end
      self.class.need(count == selected["entry_count"] &&
        digest.hexdigest == selected["retained_entries_sha256"], "DATASET_EDITION_ROWS_CHANGED")
      io.write("]}\n")
      selected
    end
  end
end

# MIT. Durable business-job receiving over the original seller and Node Buyer.
require_relative "seller_client"

module Starforge
  # Keep the key in your application's job/database record. The same key selects
  # one native intent across Active Job retries and process restarts.
  class Receiving
    attr_reader :directory, :intent_id
    def self.key_id(key)
      Files.need(key.is_a?(String) && !key.strip.empty? && key.bytesize <= 1024 &&
        key.valid_encoding?, "RUBY_BUSINESS_KEY_REQUIRED")
      Files.hash(key.b)
    end
    def self.intent_id(key)
      "ruby:" + key_id(key)
    end
    def self.received(directory:, key:, expected_manifest_sha256: nil)
      root = Files.directory(directory)
      path = Files.directory(File.join(root,key_id(key)))
      job_bytes = Files.read(File.join(path,"job.json"),131_072)
      job = Files.parse(job_bytes)
      receipt = Files.parse(Files.read(File.join(path,"received.json"),131_072))
      Files.need(job["schema"] == "stellar-forge.ruby-business-job.v1" &&
        job["keySha256"] == key_id(key) && job["intentId"] == intent_id(key) &&
        receipt["schema"] == "stellar-forge.ruby-business-received.v1" &&
        receipt["jobSha256"] == Files.hash(job_bytes) &&
        receipt["intentId"] == job["intentId"] && receipt["sourceSha256"] == job["sourceSha256"] &&
        receipt["directory"] == File.join(path,"received"), "RUBY_BUSINESS_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
      Files.need(expected_manifest_sha256.nil? || receipt["manifestSha256"] == expected_manifest_sha256,
        "RUBY_DELIVERY_MANIFEST_CHANGED")
      delivery = Delivery.open(receipt["directory"],expected_manifest_sha256: receipt.fetch("manifestSha256"))
      Files.need(delivery.manifest["intentId"] == job["intentId"] &&
        delivery.manifest["sourceSha256"] == job["sourceSha256"], "RUBY_BUSINESS_DELIVERY_CHANGED")
      delivery
    end

    def initialize(client:, buyer:, directory:, key:, bound:, response_file: nil)
      Files.need(client.is_a?(SellerClient) && buyer.is_a?(Buyer) && bound.is_a?(BoundRequest),
        "RUBY_BUSINESS_SOURCE_REQUIRED")
      @client, @buyer, @key = client, buyer, key.dup.freeze
      @root = Files.directory(directory,create: true)
      @directory = Files.directory(File.join(@root,self.class.key_id(key)),create: true)
      @intent_id = self.class.intent_id(key)
      Files.need(bound.intent_id == @intent_id && bound.source_sha256 == client.source["sourceSha256"],

          File.exist?(File.join(@directory,"prepared.json")) ? "PREPARED" : "REQUEST_RETAINED",
          "intentId"=>@intent_id,"operation"=>File.exist?(File.join(@directory,"prepared.json")) ?

      end
    end

    def receive(cancel: nil)

          "intentId"=>@intent_id,"sourceSha256"=>@bound.source_sha256,
          "directory"=>received.directory,"manifestSha256"=>received.manifest_sha256}))
        received
      end
    end
  end
